Tomato with Late Blight.symptoms: Tomato leaves and stems can develop dark lesions, sometimes with white sporulation or fuzz under humid or damp conditions. Dry conditions can leave dark lesions without visible fuzz.
immediate_actions: If late blight is suspected in a field, contact the local agricultural extension service promptly because the pathogen can spread by wind.
For localized field outbreaks, Cornell advises removing affected plants and nearby healthy plants to limit spread.
non_chemical_management: Remove and properly dispose of infected plant material; do not leave infected tomato fruit or plant debris in cull piles.
prevention: Consider resistant tomato varieties where available.
Rotate away from solanaceous crops for three years.
Scout susceptible and shaded areas regularly and check regional late-blight alerts.
Tomato with Late Blight.source_organization: Cornell University, Cornell Vegetables / New York State Integrated Pest Management
Tomato with Late Blight.region: New York, United States; confirm local guidance elsewhere.
safety_notes: This model is a screening aid, not a diagnosis. Confirm suspected late blight with an agricultural extension service.
No pesticide is recommended here. If a pesticide is considered, follow local registration, label, and extension guidance.

Potato with Late Blight.symptoms: Potato leaves and stems can develop dark lesions, sometimes with white sporulation or fuzz under humid or damp conditions. Dry conditions can leave dark lesions without visible fuzz.
immediate_actions: If late blight is suspected in a field, contact the local agricultural extension service promptly because the pathogen can spread by wind.
Dispose of infected tubers properly; Cornell notes that infected tubers can be a source of inoculum.
non_chemical_management: Do not leave infected tubers in cull piles or other places where they can produce new sources of infection.
prevention: Consider resistant potato varieties where available.
Rotate away from solanaceous crops for three years.
Scout susceptible and shaded areas regularly and check regional late-blight alerts.
